title: Homogeneous syzygies lift leading projective-order relations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\geq0$, and let $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ have all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be a prime, put $L=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $N=\mathfrak pL$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and set $\delta(\phi)=\phi(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)/1$ and $U_v=\{\phi\in B_v:\delta(\phi)\in N^v\}$ for $v\geq0$.
Let $b\geq0$, $e\geq1$, and let nonzero homogeneous forms $\phi_j\in U_{d_j}$ have degrees $1\leq d_j\leq e$ for $1\leq j\leq b$. Suppose $\beta_j\in N^{e-d_j}$ and
$$\sum_{j=1}^b\beta_j\delta(\phi_j)\in N^{e+1}.$$
Then there are a finite index set $V$, integers $1\leq h_v\leq e$, elements $a_v\in N^{e-h_v}$, and homogeneous polynomials $C_{vj}$ such that $C_{vj}=0$ when $h_v<d_j$, $C_{vj}\in U_{h_v-d_j}$ otherwise, and
$$\sum_{j=1}^b C_{vj}\phi_j=0\quad(v\in V),\qquad
\beta_j-\sum_{v\in V}a_v\delta(C_{vj})\in N^{e-d_j+1}\quad(1\leq j\leq b).$$
The zero polynomial is allowed in every homogeneous component, $N^0=L$, and an empty sum is zero.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), Lemma 17, pp.172–173, with (13.2), (14.2), (16.1)–(16.2); finite-jet form of its completed-coefficient assertion, also used in (20.4)–(20.8), pp.178–179; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: If $b=0$, take $V=\varnothing$. Otherwise apply [lem-trf-projective-order-triangular-coordinates], writing $c$ for its number of generators, to avoid confusing it with the given filtration level $e$. Permuting $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ preserves every hypothesis and conclusion, so use the resulting coordinates. Put $R=k[\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_c]=U$, with $\deg\sigma_i=q_i\ge1$. Write $\phi_j=P_j(\sigma)$, where $P_j\in k[S_1,\ldots,S_c]$ is weighted homogeneous of weight $d_j$. Indeed, separate a polynomial expression for $\phi_j$ into weights: its weight-$d_j$ component evaluates to $\phi_j$, and all other components evaluate to zero; algebraic independence of the $\sigma_i$ makes those components zero. For $c=0$, $U=k$ has no nonzero positive-degree forms, so the nonempty family cannot occur.

source.place: Agent-written finite-jet adaptation of Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities (1970), Lemma 17, printed pp.172–173, with (13.2), (14.2), (16.1)–(16.2). Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. The local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation only, not the source of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this specialized result.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-projective-order-completed-normal-form] for these coordinates. Write $\widehat N=N\widehat L$, $\rho_i=\delta(\sigma_i)$, and use its $F,\epsilon_0,z,\omega,\Delta,L_0,N_0$. Here $\epsilon_0:k\hookrightarrow F$ is the residue-induced embedding; it need not equal the original inclusion of $k$ in $\widehat L$. Expand
$$\beta_j=\sum_{A,B,\gamma}b_j(A,B,\gamma)\rho^Az^B\omega^\gamma,\qquad b_j(A,B,\gamma)\in F.$$
The order formula and $\beta_j\in N^{e-d_j}$ imply that all coefficients of weight $q\cdot A+|B|+|\gamma|<e-d_j$ vanish. Let $T_j$ be the finite sum of terms of weight exactly $e-d_j$. Finiteness follows from $q_i\ge1$, bounded $B\in\Delta$, and finite variable tuples. Then $\beta_j-T_j\in\widehat N^{e-d_j+1}$. The cited coefficient comparison gives $\delta(\phi_j)-P_j^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)\in\widehat N^{d_j+1}$. Using the assumed relation, multiplication of these congruences gives
$$\sum_jT_jP_j^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)\in\widehat N^{e+1}.$$

source.place: Agent-written finite-jet adaptation of Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities (1970), Lemma 17, printed pp.172–173, with (13.2), (14.2), (16.1)–(16.2). Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. The local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation only, not the source of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this specialized result.

proof.text:
Every term in the last finite sum has weight exactly $e$, and multiplication by a polynomial in $\rho$ leaves $B\in\Delta$ unchanged. Thus it is already a finite normal expansion. By the order formula of [lem-trf-projective-order-completed-normal-form], a nonzero such expansion has order exactly $e$. The sum is therefore zero. For each pair $(B,\gamma)$ occurring in the $T_j$, set $h=e-|B|-|\gamma|$ and
$$Q_{B\gamma,j}(S)=\sum_{q\cdot A=h-d_j}b_j(A,B,\gamma)S^A.$$
Normal-expansion uniqueness yields the polynomial identity
$$\sum_jQ_{B\gamma,j}(S)P_j^{\epsilon_0}(S)=0\quad\text{in }F[S].$$
Indeed each coefficient of $S^A$ here is precisely the coefficient of $\rho^Az^B\omega^\gamma$ in the zero normal expansion. The polynomial $Q_{B\gamma,j}$ has weight $h-d_j$, and is zero for $h<d_j$. Discard pairs for which all $Q_{B\gamma,j}$ are zero. Every retained pair has $1\le h\le e$, since some $d_j\ge1$ occurs and $|B|+|\gamma|\ge0$.

u,j}$ has weight $h-d_j$ and vanishes for $h<d_j$. Inserting these expressions into the preceding polynomial identity, the coefficient of every monomial is an $\epsilon_0(k)$-linear combination of the independent $u_

source.place: Agent-written finite-jet adaptation of Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities (1970), Lemma 17, printed pp.172–173, with (13.2), (14.2), (16.1)–(16.2). Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. The local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation only, not the source of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this specialized result.

proof.text:
For $h_v\ge d_j$, apply the coefficient comparison of [lem-trf-projective-order-completed-normal-form] to the weighted homogeneous polynomial $D_{B\gamma\nu,j}$ of weight $h_v-d_j$. It gives
$$\delta(C_{vj})-D_{B\gamma\nu,j}^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)\in\widehat N^{h_v-d_j+1}.$$
Both terms have order at least $h_v-d_j$. Thus Step 5's congruence for $a_v$ gives
$$a_v\delta(C_{vj})-u_\nu z^B\omega^\gamma D_{B\gamma\nu,j}^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)\in\widehat N^{e-d_j+1}.$$
For $h_v<d_j$ both products are zero. Summing over $V$, Step 4's coefficient expansion reconstructs exactly $T_j$. Step 2 therefore shows $\beta_j-\sum_va_v\delta(C_{vj})\in\widehat N^{e-d_j+1}$. This difference is in $L$, and the cited preservation of orders for $L\to\widehat L$ implies it belongs to $N^{e-d_j+1}$. This proves the required congruence. If every $T_j=0$, $V=\varnothing$ works. The arguments also include zero coefficients, $h_v=d_j$ (constant polynomials), $e=1$, and empty parameter tuples.
